req.title: Root endpoint responds
req.statement: The system shall serve a welcome message at GET / with HTTP 200.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states GET / must return HTTP 200 with a specific JSON payload. To achieve high mutation kill rate: (1) positive EP test asserts exact status code 200 and exact JSON keys+values; (2) negative NEG test verifies that POST / returns 405 (wrong method), confirming the handler is method-specific; (3) BVA boundary test asserts the exact string constants in the response body ('Welcome to Task Manager API', '/docs', '1.0.0') so any mutation to those literals is caught. Together these cover status-code mutations (200->201, 200->204), payload-key mutations, payload-value mutations, and method-guard mutations.

tests.name: test_root_get_returns_200_with_exact_payload
expected: Response JSON equals {"message": "Welcome to Task Manager API", "docs": "/docs", "version": "1.0.0"}

tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_root_get_returns_200_with_exact_payload():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body == {
        "message": "Welcome to Task Manager API",
        "docs": "/docs",
        "version": "1.0.0"
    }

test_root_get_returns_200_with_exact_payload()

expected: body['message'] is exactly 'Welcome to Task Manager API'

tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_root_response_exact_string_constants():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert len(body) == 3
    assert body["message"] == "Welcome to Task Manager API"
    assert body["docs"] == "/docs"
    assert body["version"] == "1.0.0"
    assert "message" in body
    assert "docs" in body
    assert "version" in body

test_root_response_exact_string_constants()
